lesson.text: Quick memory: last unit, reading closely. What is a key detail? A detail that helps show the main idea.
The central idea is the most important point a whole text makes. Every paragraph helps develop it.

Read: Many cities are planting rooftop gardens. The plants cool buildings in summer, soak up rainwater that would flood the streets, and give bees and birds new homes. Some rooftops even grow vegetables for local cafes.
The central idea: rooftop gardens make cities better places. The details (cooling, rainwater, wildlife, food) develop it.
An objective summary gives the central idea and the key details in your own words, in order, with no opinions: "I think gardens are great" doesn't belong.
Try it in the world: after a long game session, write a three-sentence summary of what you did, in order, with no opinions. Could a friend follow it? Next: plot and character.

exercises.prompt: What is a text's central idea?
exercises.hint: What is the whole text mostly about?
choices: the most important point of the whole text
exercises.explain: The central idea is the most important point the whole text makes.

exercises.prompt: In the rooftop text, what is the central idea?
exercises.hint: What do all the details add up to?
exercises.explain: Every detail shows how rooftop gardens make cities better.

exercises.prompt: An objective summary includes your own opinion.
exercises.hint: Objective means without opinions.
exercises.explain: No: an objective summary leaves opinions out.

exercises.prompt: Which detail supports the rooftop text's central idea?
exercises.hint: Which one shows a way gardens help?
choices: The plants cool buildings in summer.
exercises.explain: Cooling buildings is one way gardens make cities better.

exercises.prompt: Details help develop the central idea.
exercises.hint: Details build it up.
exercises.explain: Yes: details develop the central idea.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence belongs in an objective summary of the rooftop text?
exercises.hint: Which sentence gives the text's ideas without saying what you think?
choices: Rooftop gardens cool buildings and help nature.
Rooftop gardens are the best idea ever.
I want one on my house.
exercises.explain: It gives the text's ideas without the writer's own opinion.

exercises.prompt: A text explains how sleep helps memory, mood and growth. What is its central idea?
exercises.hint: What do memory, mood and growth have in common?
choices: Sleep matters for body and mind.
exercises.explain: All three details show that sleep matters for body and mind.

exercises.prompt: Which is NOT a key detail for a summary of a text about a new bridge?
exercises.hint: Which one isn't about the bridge?
exercises.explain: The writer's favourite colour has nothing to do with the bridge.

exercises.prompt: A summary should follow the order of the text.
exercises.hint: Keep the order.
exercises.explain: Yes: a summary follows the text's order.

exercises.prompt: Order the steps to write an objective summary.
exercises.hint: Start by reading.
exercises.explain: Read, find the central idea, choose key details, then write.

exercises.prompt: A text on volcanoes covers how they form, how scientists watch them and how towns prepare. What is the best central idea?
exercises.hint: Join all three parts.
choices: Volcanoes can be understood and prepared for.
exercises.explain: Forming, watching and preparing all show volcanoes can be understood and prepared for.

exercises.prompt: Why should a summary leave out opinions?
exercises.hint: Whose ideas does a summary show?
choices: It shows the text's ideas, not yours.
exercises.explain: A summary reports what the text says.

exercises.prompt: One paragraph is on the cost of a school trip, one on what pupils learn. What central idea could join them?
exercises.hint: Put cost and learning together.
choices: The trip costs money but teaches a lot.
exercises.explain: The central idea joins both: the trip costs money but teaches a lot.

exercises.prompt: A central idea is always stated in the first sentence.
exercises.hint: Sometimes you work it out.
exercises.explain: No: it can come anywhere, or not be stated at all.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is the most objective?
exercises.hint: Which one is only facts?
choices: The park has 40 trees and a pond.
The park is the prettiest place in town.
exercises.explain: It gives facts with no opinion.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences for a summary of the rooftop text.
items: They give birds and bees homes.
exercises.hint: A summary gives the text's key details, with no opinions.
exercises.explain: Cooling, soaking up rain and giving homes are the text's details. "I think gardens are great" and "fun to visit" are opinions.

exercises.prompt: Match each set of details to its central idea.
exercises.hint: Ask what all the details in each set add up to.
exercises.explain: Cooling, rain and wildlife: rooftop gardens help. Memory, mood and growth: sleep matters. Forming, watching and preparing: volcanoes can be prepared for.

exercises.prompt: Order a summary of the rooftop text: the central idea first, then the key details in the text's order.
items: They give bees and birds new homes.
exercises.hint: A summary keeps the text's order: what does the text say first, second and third?
exercises.explain: The central idea comes first, then the details in the text's order: cooling buildings, soaking up rainwater, then new homes for bees and birds.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: objective, or with an opinion?
exercises.hint: Could you check it with facts, or is it someone's feeling?
exercises.explain: Objective sentences can be checked: 40 trees, 5 gold, plants cooling buildings. Lovely, a waste and amazing are opinions, so they stay out of an objective summary.

exercises.prompt: How many key details does the rooftop text give to show that the gardens make cities better?
exercises.hint: List what the gardens do for the city, one by one.
exercises.explain: Cooling buildings, soaking up rainwater, homes for bees and birds, and vegetables for cafes: 4 key details, as card 3 lists them: cooling, rainwater, wildlife and food.
